proof_scope: Independent source and artifact hash audit, 8 unit tests, and first-generation 30-goal negative-control probes for three worlds at seed 11. Full 3-seed default runs were not repeated because the control requirements already fail. This receipt does not claim that the reported solve rates are false or that recursive learning is impossible.

tests.name: source/evidence hashes and scoreboard SHA-256 against manifest

counterexamples.condition: Arms must be compared on matched sealed goals to isolate the library intervention
counterexamples.finding: Both experiment scripts incorporate arm in the RNG seed, so each arm receives a different sealed exam. With seed 11, only 0–3 of 30 functions overlap across control-vs-library exams in each world.

counterexamples.condition: Random library must have equal concept sizes as the actual library
counterexamples.finding: Random generator fails exact size-matching because building binary nodes does not preserve requested total node count; the existing unit test checks only the number of concepts.

supported_findings: Candidate input sources and results are hash consistent with declared manifest
Stored analysis reports NO_COMPOUNDING, which is appropriately not a claim of compounding
limits: Candidate scores cannot support matched-control improvement claims until the same exam lists and size-matched random controls are enforced
The separate integer reference evaluator is sampled at 64 pairs, whereas the full 65536-pair check uses NumPy evaluate
No original full-default 3-seed rerun performed; blocked by reproducible experimental-design violations
repair: Precompute identical per-world/per-generation/per-seed sealed goal sets independently of arm, then compare outcomes on paired goals
Construct random library expressions with exactly equal total node sizes and match size distribution to the real library arm, with explicit tests
Rerun three-seed full experiment and curriculum under frozen common exams, verify CPU/candidate budgets and independently validate verdicts
